tells.1: The impersonal policy phrasing 'the $135 rate applies to you too' reads as stiff rather than conversational.
tells.2: The phrase 'when the new rate starts for you' is slightly unnatural.
tells.3: The formal wording 'when the new $135 rate will take effect for you' feels over-polished and corporate.

reason: Version 4 sounds the most natural and human while staying clear and warm, especially with 'then move to $135' and 'so you'll have more options.'
